citation: Morton et al., 2018, British Journal of Sports Medicine (meta-analysis, 49 studies)
finding: Protein intakes up to ~1.6g/kg/day maximize resistance-training-induced gains in muscle mass; higher intakes (up to 2.2g/kg/day) show benefit for lean individuals in a calorie deficit.

citation: Schoenfeld & Aragon, 2018, Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
finding: ~0.4g/kg per meal across 3-4 meals/day maximizes muscle protein synthesis versus skewed distribution.

citation: Vilar-Gomez et al., 2015, Gastroenterology
finding: ≥7% body weight loss resolves NASH in most patients; ≥10% loss can regress fibrosis. Weight loss is the single most effective intervention for fatty liver.

topic: NAFLD — exercise independent of weight loss
citation: Hashida et al., 2017, Journal of Hepatology (systematic review)
finding: Aerobic and resistance exercise reduce intrahepatic fat even without significant weight loss, via improved insulin sensitivity.

citation: EASL-EASD-EASO Clinical Practice Guidelines, 2016 (updated 2024)
finding: First-line management is lifestyle: calorie deficit, reduced saturated fat/added sugar, increased fibre, ≥150min/week moderate aerobic activity, resistance training 2-3x/week, and alcohol minimization.

citation: Zelber-Sagi et al., 2018, Liver International
finding: Fructose-sweetened beverages are independently associated with liver fat accumulation regardless of total calorie intake.

citation: Mandsager et al., 2018, JAMA Network Open (122,007 patients)
finding: Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 max) shows a continuous, dose-dependent inverse association with all-cause mortality — the strongest modifiable predictor of longevity studied.

citation: Momma et al., 2022, British Journal of Sports Medicine (meta-analysis)
finding: Muscle-strengthening activity 30-60 min/week associated with 10-20% lower all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality; more is not better beyond ~60min/week.

citation: Milanović et al., 2015, Sports Medicine (meta-analysis)
finding: High-intensity interval training produces larger VO2 max improvements than moderate continuous training in the same time budget.

citation: Seiler, 2010, International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
finding: Elite endurance athletes improve most with ~80% low-intensity (Zone 2) / ~20% high-intensity training rather than moderate-intensity-heavy plans.

citation: Cappuccio et al., 2010, Sleep (meta-analysis, 1.3M participants)
finding: Both short (<6h) and long (>9h) sleep associated with increased mortality; 7-8h is the low-risk range for adults.

citation: Watson et al., 2015, joint consensus statement, American Academy of Sleep Medicine & Sleep Research Society
finding: Adults should sleep 7+ hours per night on a regular basis for optimal health.

citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on NAFLD, 2016
finding: Even moderate alcohol intake accelerates fibrosis progression in patients with existing fatty liver; abstinence or near-abstinence is advised.

citation: WHO Expert Consultation, 2004, The Lancet
finding: For Asian populations, health risk rises at lower BMI than the standard scale: overweight ≥23 kg/m², obese ≥27.5 kg/m² (vs 25/30 on the standard WHO scale).

citation: Plews et al., 2013, Sports Medicine (review)
finding: A declining rolling 7-day HRV average relative to baseline is a validated signal for reducing training load; day-to-day HRV alone is noisy and should be trended, not read in isolation.

citation: Ma et al., 2018, Journal of Hepatology
finding: Higher dietary fibre intake is independently associated with lower odds of NAFLD, largely via improved insulin sensitivity and gut microbiome effects.

citation: Mifflin et al., 1990, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
finding: The Mifflin-St Jeor equation (men: 10×weight[kg] + 6.25×height[cm] − 5×age + 5) is the most accurate validated BMR estimate for the general population, used as the baseline for calorie targets here.

topic: Deficit size for fat loss while preserving muscle
citation: Helms, Zinn, Rowlands & Aragon, 2014, International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
finding: A moderate ~20-25% calorie deficit below maintenance, combined with adequate protein and resistance training, better preserves lean mass during fat loss than aggressive deficits.

citation: UK Chief Medical Officers' Physical Activity Guidelines, 2019 (GOV.UK)
finding: Adults should accumulate ≥150 min/week moderate-intensity activity or ≥75 min/week vigorous activity (or an equivalent combination), plus muscle-strengthening activity on 2+ days/week, and minimise sedentary time.

citation: NICE Guideline NG49 — Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: assessment and management, 2016 (reviewed 2024)
finding: NAFLD affects an estimated 20-30% of the general population, with 2-3% having NASH (non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, the more severe inflammatory form) — Marshall's flag is a common finding, not a rare one, but still warrants the lifestyle intervention this guideline sets out as first-line.

citation: UK Chief Medical Officers' Low Risk Drinking Guidelines, 2016 (GOV.UK)
finding: To keep health risks low, adults should drink no more than 14 units/week on a regular basis, spread over 3+ days — the same limit for men and women. Given an existing fatty liver flag, staying well under this (or abstaining) is the more relevant target (see EASL guidance above).

citation: NHS Digital, Health Survey for England 2024
finding: 30% of English adults were living with obesity (BMI ≥30) in 2024 — the highest on record — and 66% were overweight or obese overall; prevalence is higher in men (67%) than women (60%) and rises with age and deprivation. Useful population context, not an individual diagnosis.

citation: SACN (Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition), Carbohydrates and Health, 2015, adopted by UK Government
finding: Free sugars should not exceed 5% of total dietary energy intake for adults and children 2+ — roughly 30g/day (about 7 sugar cubes) for an adult. Particularly relevant given fructose/added sugar's direct link to liver fat (see NAFLD entries above).

citation: SACN / Public Health England, Eatwell Guide reference values
finding: UK adults should aim for 30g/day of fibre — roughly 5 portions of fruit/veg, 2 wholewheat cereal biscuits, 2 thick slices of wholemeal bread, and a jacket potato with skin. Most UK adults currently fall short of this.

topic: UK sedentary-population protein RNI (baseline, not athletic target)
citation: UK Reference Nutrient Intake (RNI), Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition / British Nutrition Foundation
finding: The UK RNI for protein is 0.75g/kg/day for sedentary adults (~56g/day for a 75kg man) — this is a minimum to avoid deficiency, not a target for someone resistance training in a calorie deficit. The 1.6-2.2g/kg range (Morton et al., 2018, above) is the relevant figure for that goal; the RNI is cited here only to explain why generic 'UK guideline' protein numbers look much lower than the coach's target.

citation: ONS (Office for National Statistics), Health state life expectancies, UK: 2022 to 2024
finding: UK males at birth can expect 60.7 years (about 77% of total life expectancy) in good general health — both figures at their lowest since ONS records began in 2011-2013. Frames why longevity-focused habits (VO2max, resistance training, liver health) compound rather than just extending lifespan.
